question.text: Does the SleepWell online CBT-I program reduce insomnia severity in adults?
question.interpretation: Read as: the SleepWell program specifically, with evidence on online CBT-I in general as context.
question.intervention_or_exposure: SleepWell online cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia

scope.context: An employee-benefits team choosing a digital sleep program.

bottom_line: One randomized trial of SleepWell (n = 200) found a clear drop in insomnia severity against a waitlist, ISI mean difference -5.3 (95% CI -7.2 to -3.4) [P2]. A 2025 meta-analysis of online CBT-I in general found a moderate to large effect across nine trials, but it does not include SleepWell [P1]. Certainty for SleepWell itself is low: one trial, a waitlist comparison and no follow-up past nine weeks.

studies.authors: Okonkwo N, Lind M, Ferreira R
studies.title: Online cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials
studies.finding: Online CBT-I beat waitlist or usual care. Heterogeneity was substantial. SleepWell is not among the nine included trials.

studies.title: SleepWell online CBT-I for insomnia: a randomized trial
studies.finding: Nine-week trial against a waitlist, registered as SW-2022-014. Registered primary outcome reported.

studies.authors: Daniels O, Rask E, Tran H
studies.title: Does age moderate the effect of online CBT-I? A secondary analysis of the SleepWell trial
studies.finding: Age 18 to 39 (n = 82): MD -6.0 (95% CI -8.9 to -3.1). Age 40 or older (n = 118): MD -4.8 (95% CI -7.3 to -2.3). Interaction p = 0.41, so no evidence age changes the effect.

synthesis.agreement: The one SleepWell trial and the wider online CBT-I meta-analysis point the same way: online CBT-I lowers insomnia severity against waitlist or usual care.
synthesis.disagreement: The size differs: the SleepWell trial's MD of -5.3 on the ISI is not directly comparable to the meta-analysis's SMD of -0.76 without a conversion, and none is made here.
synthesis.likely_reasons: Different comparison conditions, outcome scales and follow-up lengths.

evidence.reason: One trial (P2, with its secondary analysis P3 counted once). Waitlist comparison, which tends to overstate behavioral effects. Short follow-up.

evidence.outcome: Insomnia severity, online CBT-I in general
evidence.reason: A meta-analysis of nine randomized trials with substantial heterogeneity; indirect to SleepWell, which it does not include.

measures: Insomnia Severity Index (ISI): 0 to 28, lower is better; validated for self-report, sensitive to change but not a diagnosis.
gaps: No trial compares SleepWell with an active control or in-person CBT-I.
No follow-up beyond nine weeks, so durability is unknown.
No data on shift workers or on people with comorbid depression.
ClinicalTrials.gov holds no record: the trial's registration (SW-2022-014) is in another registry.
implications: For an employee-benefits team, the evidence supports that online CBT-I as a class lowers insomnia severity, and that SleepWell has one positive trial. It does not show SleepWell beats other programs or that the gain lasts. A review of the trial's registered protocol against the paper would be a reasonable next check.
report_markdown:
## Bottom line
One randomized trial of SleepWell (n = 200) found a clear drop in insomnia severity against a waitlist, ISI mean difference -5.3 (95% CI -7.2 to -3.4) [P2]. A 2025 meta-analysis of online CBT-I in general found a moderate to large effect across nine trials but does not include SleepWell [P1]. Certainty for SleepWell itself is low.

## Search strategy
Run 2026-11-14 on Crossref, PubMed, Europe PMC and ClinicalTrials.gov, scope 2018 to 2026, randomized trials and systematic reviews, adults. Hits: Crossref 3, PubMed 2, Europe PMC 2, ClinicalTrials.gov 0.

## Key studies
| Paper | Design | n | Finding | Effect (95% CI) | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Okonkwo 2025 [P1] | meta-analysis, 9 trials | 2,840 | online CBT-I beats waitlist or usual care | SMD -0.76 (-0.95 to -0.57) | |
| Rask 2023 [P2] | RCT | 200 | SleepWell beats waitlist at 9 weeks | MD -5.3 (-7.2 to -3.4) | |
| Daniels 2024 [P3] | secondary analysis of P2 | same 200 | no age interaction (p = 0.41) | -6.0 and -4.8 by age | same trial as P2 |

## Synthesis
The SleepWell trial and the meta-analysis agree in direction. Their effect sizes use different scales and are not compared.

## Evidence strength
| Outcome | Certainty | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| ISI at 9 weeks, SleepWell | low | one trial counted once, waitlist control, short follow-up |
| Insomnia severity, online CBT-I in general | moderate | meta-analysis, heterogeneity, indirect to SleepWell |

## Gaps
No active-control trial, no follow-up beyond nine weeks, no shift-worker data.

## Implications for the stated context
The evidence supports online CBT-I as a class and gives SleepWell one positive trial. It does not show SleepWell is better than other programs or that the gain lasts.
